system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: `@llm_behavior` with structured output, frame-aware prompt construction, cost accounting.
system_prompt_style.note: Prompts are pack-supplied templates rendered per behavior; no explicit render line in the provided evidence.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: a view of the graph, and a context handle
env_context_strategy.note: Context is a scoped graph view, not repository/file context; no file-tree or retrieval mechanism in evidence.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Replay cost grows with log length, so very long-lived runs eventually need checkpointing or compaction, which we do not yet provide
context_compaction.note: v1.5 mentions 'compaction phase 1 (snapshot + archive tier ...)' for the event store, not for LLM context.

observation_format.evidence_quote: a tool response is keyed on the tool name and a deterministic hash of its arguments
observation_format.note: Tool/LLM responses are logged as text payload events; no image modality in evidence.

tool_call_format.note: Provider tool use: 'the side-by-side surface, including tool use and provider-specific token counting'.

tool_count.evidence_quote:
The bundled
[Diligence pack](activegraph/packs/diligence) is the reference:
8 object types, 7 behaviors, 3 tools, recorded fixtures.
tool_count.note: Default bundled Diligence pack ships 3 tools.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: A pack bundles object types, behaviors, tools, prompts, and policies for a specific domain.
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing primitive; agent mutates graph objects via patches, not files.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: a model response is keyed on a hash of the entire request (system message, user messages, model identifier, tool definitions, and output schema)
tool_schema_source.note: Tools declared with the `@tool` decorator inside packs; schema source not shown explicitly.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote:
Two hard dependencies (`click` for the CLI, `pydantic`
for the pack format); persistence backends and provider integrations
are opt-in extras.
protocol_standardization.note: No MCP/A2A mention anywhere in the provided evidence.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote:
There is no top-level script sequencing the steps of
a run.
loop_primitives.note: Behaviors react to events on a shared graph; event_driven is the default and primary loop.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: a planner behavior reacts to a goal by creating a company; a question-generator reacts to the company by emitting research questions
planning_granularity.note: Plan is materialized as typed task/question objects in the persisted graph.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote:
Behaviors react to a shared graph instead of talking
to each other.
multi_agent_topology.note: Blackboard-style: multiple independent LLM-backed behaviors coordinate only through the shared graph.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote:
No component
instructs another; coordination happens entirely through the shared graph.
delegation_mechanism.note: Shared event log/graph acts as the bus; no direct spawn or handoff.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote:
**Policies** — approval and gating for behavior capabilities. Which
  behaviors can call which tools, which mutations require human
  approval, what the runtime refuses.
human_in_loop.note: `approval.proposed` / `approval.granted` event types; policies are per-pack configurable.

short_term_state.evidence_quote:
An event-sourced reactive graph runtime for long-running, auditable,
agentic systems. Behaviors react to a shared graph instead of talking
to each other.
short_term_state.note: Working state is a shared typed graph (objects/relations such as task with status fields) plus event log, not a message list; README also lists frames with goal, constraints, budget. Coded from README prose; no line numbers available in excerpts.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote:
full event-log persistence, save/load across processes,
  fork from any historical event, structural diff between runs
long_term_memory.note: SQLite/Postgres event store holds prior runs; reinjection across runs happens via load/fork rather than retrieval.

state_persistence.evidence_quote:
Every run is resumable,
forkable, and diff-able from its event log.

self_verification.evidence_quote: detects contradictions, identifies risks, and synthesizes a memo
self_verification.note: Diligence pack has contradiction-detection and a confidence_threshold_for_review behavior; no harness-run tests or linters.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: bounded LLM retries for transient provider failures
retry_policy.note: Only transport-level LLM retries; no task-level retry policy. Fork→test→promote is an operator loop, not automatic.

rollback.evidence_quote:
compaction phase 1 (snapshot + archive tier + the
  retention pin set, never deletion)
rollback.note: Log is append-only; rejected patches are events, but no revert of executed side effects. Fork gives counterfactual branching, not rollback.

termination_condition.evidence_quote:
the runtime's defense is
a per-run budget (caps on events, behavior calls, model calls, patches, recursion depth, wall-clock
time, and cost)
termination_condition.note: Also `runtime.idle` (queue empty) ends a run; wall-clock cap noted under F3.

cost_controls.evidence_quote:
caps on events, behavior calls, model calls, patches, recursion depth, wall-clock
time, and cost
cost_controls.note: Content-addressed LLM/tool response cache serves replay and fork prefixes.

timeouts.note: Also quantum-level `max_seconds=0.25` for cooperative yielding; no per-tool timeout found.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote:
the provider-neutral `TrialExecutor` seam with the existing
  local subprocess as its honest, non-security-sandbox default
execution_isolation.note: Behaviors run in-process in the host runtime; the subprocess executor applies only to fork trials.

permission_model.evidence_quote:
Which
  behaviors can call which tools, which mutations require human
  approval, what the runtime refuses.
permission_model.note: Pack policies gate behavior→tool capability; `Pack.capabilities` is declarative.

tracing.note: Opt-in extra `activegraph[opentelemetry]`; the structured event log/trace is always on.

replayability.evidence_quote: Two replays of the same log produce deterministically identical state.
replayability.note: Strict replay fails on divergence; determinism is a property of re-projecting an existing log.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote:
We report
no large-scale empirical evaluation of task performance
eval_hooks.note: Ships fixtures and a deterministic quickstart snapshot test, but no benchmark evaluation runner.

guardrails.evidence_quote: **Policies** — approval and gating for behavior capabilities.
guardrails.note: Also fail-closed direct `web_fetch` (v1.8) and a closed env allow-list for trial children.

target_domain.evidence_quote:
The diligence pack performs investment due
diligence: from a company name it generates research questions, researches each against a document
store
target_domain.note: General-purpose runtime; bundled reference pack is investment-research.

open_source.evidence_quote: Active Graph is licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote:
Both LLM providers expose the same `LLMProvider` Protocol surface;
swap one for the other without touching `@llm_behavior` definitions.
